title: Backfill & Replay Tooling for Console Analytics Pipeline (replayer service)
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build a resilient, auditable, and cost-controlled replayer/backfill service to support reprocessing of console usage events and derived analytics. The goal is to allow targeted replays (by tenant, route, time window, or event type) against downstream analytics stacks (warehouse jobs, feature stores, and observability dashboards) with strong guarantees: idempotence, deduplication, schema-evolution handling, and operations tooling (progress tracking, pause/resume, error inspection, throughput throttling).
tasks: Design API and CLI for replayer: start/stop/resume/status/cancel with filters (tenant, model, route, event_type, time range)
Implement controlled Kafka/Cloud Pub/Sub consumer for replay that supports adjustable concurrency and rate limits
Add idempotency metadata and watermarking to replayed messages to avoid double-counting in downstream aggregations
Produce translation layer for schema evolution: mapping rules + fallback on unknown fields
Wire replayer outputs to two targets: analytics-warehouse ingestion topic and metrics pipeline (Prometheus/Tempo) for dashboard rebuilds
Build audit and progress dashboard in Console: jobs, processed counts, error samples, estimated time remaining
Create operator runbook and CLI helpers for common backfills (tenant-wide, retention reprocessing, bugfix re-runs)
Cost estimation module: estimate bytes processed, compute hours, and S3/BigQuery costs for proposed run
Add automated safety checks: max-events cap, concurrency ceiling per tenant, data retention constraints
Write integration tests with local replay fixture and end-to-end test against staging warehouse
acceptance_criteria: Replayer can start a job that replays events for a given tenant and time window and completes successfully on staging
Downstream aggregations reflect identical results to original processing for a controlled test dataset (within tolerated nondeterminism)
Duplicate prevention: replaying the same time window twice does not increment aggregation counters beyond first run
Operators can pause/resume/cancel jobs and inspect a job's error sample and per-partition progress from the Console UI
Safety checks prevent accidental full-cluster replays without explicit confirmation and quota override
Cost estimate returned before job kickoff and job created with an associated billing tag for accounting
notes: Trade-offs considered: implementing reprocessing as a batch job vs streaming replayer. Chosen approach: streaming-replayer that reads archival storage (S3) + optional Kafka offsets for lower tail-latency; streaming allows throttling and better observability, at cost of complexity for ordering/deduplication.

Deduplication design: add replay_run_id and original_event_id headers, use idempotent inserts in warehouse via upsert keys (tenant_id, event_id, event_timestamp) and maintain short-lived replay_blacklist to guard high-traffic windows.

Schema evolution: create a mapping layer that can drop unknown fields, rename keys per a ruleset stored in Console config. For major schema changes require a dry-run mode that writes to a 'staging' table for manual validation before flipping target alias.
Backpressure strategy: honor downstream ingestion throughput; implement token-bucket rate limiter per tenant and per-output to avoid overwhelming BigQuery load jobs and metrics exporters.

Security constraints: replay service must run in Private network for on-prem customers and use customer KMS keys when writing decrypted payloads. Security review requested to validate logging of PII and KMS usage.

Cost considerations: reprocessing large windows can be expensive. We'll enforce default max-events and provide a preflight cost estimate. For large enterprise backfills we recommend Dedicated cluster scheduling with reserved capacity.
Metrics to capture: events_processed, events_failed, bytes_read, bytes_written, downstream_failures, job_duration_seconds, estimated_cost_usd
comments: 2026-02-15 Ava Martinez: Created ticket after spike. Spike showed archived events are split between S3 partitioned shards and Kafka long-term topic. Next step: decide canonical replay source. Suggest S3 primary + Kafka for near-term smaller windows.

2026-02-20 Liam Chen: Prototype consumer built that reads S3 parquet shards and emits to replay topic. Found challenge: parquet files contain mixed schema versions. Implemented schema normalization layer that flattens unknown fields to a metadata blob.

2026-02-26 Paul Singh (Data Eng): Requested idempotency guarantees from warehouse ingestion. Proposed approach: use MERGE statements on BigQuery with primary key (tenant,event_id) and event_sequence to keep last-write semantics. Need to ensure performance for high-volume runs.

2026-03-02 Maria Gomez (PM): Prioritized support for per-tenant replays and added requirement for cost estimate preflight. Also requested UI to surface a sample of first 10 failed events for operator debugging.

2026-03-05 Design feedback (Keisha Patel): Console job list should show 'safety_score' and 'estimated_cost' columns. Recommended a confirmation modal that requires typing tenant name for large (>10M events) runs.

2026-03-07 Liam Chen: Implemented proof-of-concept CLI 'replayer run' with flags for --tenant --from --to --max-events. Hooked into staging warehouse; end-to-end test passed for a 1M event window but observed 12% longer processing due to MERGE overhead. Looking into batching upsert keys to reduce commit count.

2026-03-09 Security (Jordan Lee): Flagged that replay logs inadvertently included user_email in debug logs. Patch submitted to redact PII; requires security review before enabling replay in private clusters.

2026-03-10 Ava Martinez: Merged initial PR for schema normalization and CLI. Next milestones: implement idempotent warehouse writes, build Console job dashboard, and complete security review. Reassigning remaining work to sprint 2026-W11 for rollout prep.
